events.title: AWS Student Builder Group UCC Launch: Your Cloud Journey Starts Here
events.summary: The online launch of the group: who we are, the basics of cloud computing, and advice on getting started from guest speaker Isaac Tandoh.

review.notes: No end time in any source. endsAt equals startsAt, so the site shows the start time only. Body follows the recap (S6); the announced live Q&A is not claimed.

events.body:
## Day One

We launched the AWS Student Builder Group at University of Cape Coast on Google Meet, for students interested in cloud computing, AWS, DevOps and technology more widely. It was free, and no AWS experience was needed.

We introduced the group, explained why we were starting it and what students could expect, and shared the activities we had planned. Then we went through the fundamentals of cloud computing.

## Guest speaker

Isaac Tandoh, AWS Cloud Trainer and DevOps Engineer, talked about how cloud and AWS are used in real work, where DevOps fits, and how students can start learning. Matthew Ntsiful also joined us and shared some of his own experience and encouragement.

Our recap ended: "Day One is officially in the books. Now, we build!"

events.summary: Nathaniel Agbenyenu on AWS certifications, cloud career paths and the skills that matter beyond the exam.

events.body:
## About the session

Our second event was about turning an interest in cloud computing into a plan. It was built around the AWS certification pathway, from Foundational to Associate, Professional and Specialty, and the careers and opportunities open to students, starting from wherever they are now.

## Guest speaker

Nathaniel Agbenyenu: Senior DevOps Engineer, Cloud Security and FinOps Lead at IT Consortium, and Co-Lead of AWS User Group Accra.

## What we talked about

- AWS certifications and where they fit
- Career paths in cloud computing
- The skills that matter beyond certifications
- Opportunities for students who want to work in cloud

The point that stood out: certifications can be part of the path, but they are not the goal. Practical skills, experience and steady learning matter just as much. Nathaniel closed with a simple reminder: "We don't give up over here."

events.body:
## About the session

An online welcome for the freshers who had just joined the group, and for any UCC student new to AWS or cloud computing. No experience was needed.

## What happened

We introduced the community, what we want to build at UCC and the opportunities we are working on for students. Core team members Kelvin Opoku and Evans Opoku then took everyone through the fundamentals of cloud computing, using simple analogies and real-world examples.

## On the agenda

- What AWS is and what you can do with it
- Why cloud skills matter for students
- AWS certifications and career opportunities
- A short live demo on AWS
- Getting started with AWS Builder Center
- What is coming next in the group

From our recap: "You don't have to know everything before you start. What matters is your willingness to learn, practise, collaborate, and keep building."

events.body:
## About the session

From Code to Cloud was our first in-person build session, in the Computer Lab at the New Science Annex. The idea was to take a personal portfolio from a folder on your laptop to a live website on AWS, then connect it to a server of your own. We got into the lab half an hour late, at 10:00 AM, so we finished at 2:00 PM instead of 1:00 PM.

## What we did

- Joel Anarba Amuni, our group leader, introduced the group, and people signed up to AWS Builder Center with the group's invite link.
- Joel then covered what cloud computing and AWS are, the Europe (Ireland) Region, the two services for the day, Amazon S3 and Amazon EC2, and how to stay safe on AWS.
- Lab 1, led by Kelvin Opoku Boateng: participants put their own name, bio and projects into the starter portfolio, created an S3 bucket, uploaded the files, switched on website hosting and opened their live link.
- Then we broke the sites on purpose. Kelvin caused an Access Denied error, and the room read the error and fixed the bucket policy.
- Lab 2: participants launched an Amazon EC2 instance from a startup script, put its address in the site's config.js and uploaded it again, so the visit counter and guestbook on their portfolio ran from their own server.
- A 20-question Wayground quiz over refreshments. The top three win group swag, which we hand over when it arrives.
- A group photo, and a reminder to terminate the EC2 instances so they stop running. The websites stay live.

posts.title: Our first website on Amazon S3
posts.excerpt: Week 3 of the bootcamp: compute and storage, a Hostel Finder website on Amazon S3, a fight with bucket policies, and a Kahoot to finish.
posts.author: AWS SBG UCC

review.notes: Session date Sat 31 Oct 2026 is derived from the post timestamp and photo filenames; Joel approved publishing on 11 Nov 2026. The body does not state the date.

posts.body:
## From concepts to a working website

In week 3 of the Zero to Cloud Practitioner bootcamp, we started with compute and storage, using real-life examples to show where each service fits in an everyday application. Then came the lab: deploying a Hostel Finder website on Amazon S3 and making it reachable on the internet.

## Learning through the errors

It was not smooth sailing. Some configurations and bucket policies tripped people up, and participants worked through them with troubleshooting and help from each other. By the end of the session, every participant had the website live.

## A podium to finish

We closed with a Kahoot quiz on everything from the first three weeks. Everyone who made the podium took home AWS swag.

## Next

The following Saturday was set for more compute services: Amazon EC2 and AWS Lambda, through practical examples.

The original post is on [our LinkedIn page](https://www.linkedin.com/company/aws-ucc/posts/).

posts.title: Certifications are part of the path, not the goal
posts.excerpt: Notes from our second event: Nathaniel Agbenyenu on certifications, cloud careers and the skills that matter beyond them.
posts.author: AWS SBG UCC

review.notes: Written from the LinkedIn recap. No attendance figure stated.

posts.body:
## The conversation

On Saturday 26 September 2026, Nathaniel Agbenyenu took the community through AWS certifications, cloud career paths, the skills that matter beyond certifications, and the opportunities open to students who want to work in cloud computing.

## The point that stuck

Certifications can be part of the path. They are not the end goal. Building practical skills, getting real experience and learning continuously matter just as much.

## The closing line

"We don't give up over here."

## What came next

We went on to run freshers onboarding in October and to start the Zero to Cloud Practitioner bootcamp with CITSA.

[See the event](/events/building-your-aws-career)

## Our first gathering

On Saturday 22 August 2026, the group held its launch on Google Meet at 8:00 PM. We introduced the community, the basics of cloud computing, and our plans for students to learn and build together.

## Learning from people in the field

Guest speaker Isaac Tandoh, AWS Cloud Trainer and DevOps Engineer, shared practical advice on starting out. Matthew Ntsiful also contributed his experience and encouragement.

## What came next

A careers talk in September, freshers onboarding in October, the Zero to Cloud Practitioner bootcamp with CITSA, and our first in-person build session, From Code to Cloud, in November.

[See the launch event](/events/aws-sbg-ucc-launch)
